item.title: Canadiens Could Break Up Detroit’s Larkin Trade With Minnesota
item.description: Danila Yurov has been one of the potential centerpieces in a possible Dylan Larkin trade between the Detroit Red Wings and the Minnesota Wild. The 22-year-old right wing is the young forward Minnesota keeps putting into its offers, and he is the piece those talks keep getting stuck on. Minnesota general manager Bill Guerin could pivot to other options if Detroit keeps playing hardball. Could Yurov be traded to a different team instead? Oct 29, 2026; Saint Paul, Minnesota, USA; New York Islanders forward Casey Cizikas (53) skates with the puck in front of Minnesota Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt (30) and forward Danila Yurov (22) in the third period at Grand Casino Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Montreal Canadiens Could Pivot From Larkin to Danila Yurov The Montreal Canadiens have been interested in trading for Larkin, but Larkin has not cleared them as a destination. TSN Hockey Insider Pierre LeBrun reported in October that Larkin’s approved trade list had grown to 10 teams and still “does not include Montreal at this point.” That leaves the Canadiens hunting for a center they can actually get. Nestor Quixtan of heavy.com thinks that Montreal could potentially go after Yurov in a trade assuming Larkin does not work out for them. Quixtan wrote , “Yurov is another intriguing possibility. The Minnesota Wild forward has reportedly been discussed as a major piece in Minnesota’s pursuit of Larkin. That alone tells us he is viewed as a valuable young asset, even if the Wild would be reluctant to move him for anything other than a significant upgrade.” If Montreal were to acquire Yurov instead of Larkin, it would pull Minnesota’s most talked-about trade chip off the board and foil Detroit’s potential plans to send Larkin to the Wild. Detroit Has Already Balked at a Yurov-Centered Offer Detroit is not sold on Yurov as the headline piece coming back. Daily Faceoff’s Anthony Di Marco reported on Oct. 30 that the Wild “have been dangling center Danila Yurov as the centerpiece of a trade; clearly that hasn’t moved the needle enough for the Red Wings,” and that one assistant general manager told the outlet that Yurov and prospect Charlie Stramel “aren’t going to net the Wild Larkin.” TSN’s Darren Dreger has put interim general manager Shawn Horcoff’s asking price at two “A”-quality prospects, an NHL-ready top-nine forward and a first-round pick. A Dylan Larkin Trade Without Yurov Changes Detroit’s Return If Detroit were to miss out on Yurov, there is a good chance that the Red Wings would either have to take just draft picks from the Wild for Larkin, or they would have to look elsewhere to trade him. There is no doubt that Detroit wants young talent in return for Larkin. Minnesota and Detroit have not agreed to any trade yet for him. Take Yurov out of the conversation and the Wild may not have a package left worth Detroit’s time.

item.title: Las Cruces teams set for 2026 high school football playoffs
item.description: The 2026 11-man high school football playoff brackets in New Mexico have been set for Classes 2A-6A. The brackets were announced on Sunday, Nov. 1. Here is a look at the Las Cruces area teams in the playoffs, which begin Nov. 6-7 with the first round. Class 6A Centennial is seeded No. 4 and has a bye in the first round. The Hawks will play the winner of No. 5 Sandia and No. 12 Farmington in the quarterfinals. The Hawks are 6-4 this season. Las Cruces High, which is 7-3, drew the No. 8 seed and will play No. 9 Rio Rancho High School (5-5) at 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6 at the Field of Dreams. Las Cruces High defeated RRHS, 14-7, in the season opener. The winner plays No. 1 Rio Rancho Cleveland in the quarterfinals. Class 5A Chaparral (4-6) is seeded No. 12 and will play at No. 5 Alamogordo (6-4). The game is scheduled for 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6. The winner will play No. 4 Los Lunas in the quarterfinals. Gadsden (7-3) is seeded No. 6 and will entertain No. 11 Mayfield (2-8) at 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6. Gadsden defeated Mayfield, 56-21, earlier this season. The winner will visit No. 3 Artesia in the quarterfinals. Class 3A Hatch Valley (4-6) is seeded No. 11 and will play at No. 6 Kirtland Central (7-2) at 1 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 7. The winner plays No. 3 Silver in the quarterfinals. 8-man football Mesilla Valley Christian (8-2) is seeded No. 4 in the 8-man division and will play No. 5 Magdalena (8-1) at 7 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 6 at Hatch Valley High School. MVCS defeated Magdalena, 56-20, in the regular season. Felix F. Chavez can be reached at fchavez@elpasotimes.com; @Fchavezeptimes on X This article originally appeared on Las Cruces Sun-News: Las Cruces teams set for 2026 high school football playoffs

item.title: Michigan paying search firm $250K to find new athletic director
item.description: The University of Michigan is prepared to a pay consultants $250,000 to help find the Ann Arbor-based school's replacement for controversial departing Director of Athletics Warde Manuel . The university tasked TurnkeyZRG, a well-known New Jersey firm, to track down candidates to the lead the school's embattled athletics department, according to contract documents obtained by the Free Press. Ultimately, new school President C. Cybele Raver and the university Board of Regents will pick the next athletic director, but the firm will provide candidates. The agreement, signed in late September, expands on a previous arrangement already in place between the school and consulting firm. The university used the same firm to hire Manuel, former basketball coach Dusty May and in the search for current head football coach Kyle Whittingham. "Candidate confidentiality will be maintained throughout the process, consistent with applicable law and university policy, to ensure a robust candidate pool," reads part of a university statement announcing the commencement of the search. Turnkey received $90,000 at the start of the deal, another $85,000 30 days after the start of the search and is owed a final $75,000 60 days after the start of the search or when a new athletic director is picked, whichever happens first. The search officially started Oct. 1, 2026, two months before Manuel is set to leave. In theory, that means the school might have a new athletic director by the end of the year. Manuel is supposed to help with the transition to a new athletic director. But it's unclear when that new person will be in place, or who might serve as interim athletic director in the meantime. Manuel's departure comes after 11 years the helm, a tenure marked by both national championships and marquee scandals. The school announced he would leave this summer on the same day it released what was described as a summary of findings from a private law firm's $12 million review of the culture of the athletic department. Manuel was the face of the department during a run of unprecedented athletic success, including national championships in both football in January 2024 and men’s basketball earlier this year. However, the investigation by law firm Jenner and Block into the department’s culture and its handling of the firing of former football coach Sherrone Moore found there were gaps in his leadership. RELATED: Sherrone Moore told of alleged rape in 2024, per Ann Arbor police report The timing of this search is particularly important for U-M athletics, given the football program has trudged through an underwhelming campaign, currently at 5-3 as it enters the final month of the regular season. Whittingham was hired last December, but some on the outside have called into question the direction of the program under the leadership of a new head coach who turns 67 later this month. item.title: Glasgow 2026 generated £233m - is it a blueprint for future games?
item.description: Josh Kerr was one of the athletes who won gold at Glasgow 2026 [Getty Images] More than a million people attended the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow this summer, and 510 million sports fans watched from around the world, according to a new report. The Glasgow 2026 impact evaluation also found that it generated £233m in economic activity across Scotland, with £158.6m of that in the host city itself. Glasgow stepped in to host a scaled-down version of the event , which featured fewer sports and athletes, after the Australian state of Victoria pulled out due to rising costs in 2024. Organisers promised it would cost the taxpayer nothing and the figures in the new report show they achieved this. Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games Some 2,749 athletes across the 74 Commonwealth nations took part in 10 sports and six para-sports. Over 11 days in July and August, six world records and 152 Commonwealth Games records were set. The overall cost of the games was less than £160m, according to the report. The majority of this money, about £100m, was funded privately by the Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF) , with the remainder coming from a range of commercial revenues such as ticket sales, broadcast rights, commercial sponsorship and merchandise. And it found that community activity linked to the games reached all of Scotland's local authorities. The games also supported 2,400 full-time equivalent years of employment, with 82 students securing games-time roles. Phil Batty, chief executive of Glasgow 2026, told the BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast : "Glasgow has demonstrated that there is a template for designing an event differently. "I think what is really unique here is that we have used the assets of the place. The amazing venues, the skilled workforce, the communities that must came alive through the course of the 11 days. That's the key here. "So yes, it has been done for less than £160m but there's so many benefits for that." Judo was among the sports featured in the Glasgow Games [Getty Images] A report into the 2014 Commonwealth Games, held in Glasgow 12 years earlier, found that version of the event cost a considerably higher £543m. The Scottish government and Glasgow City Council provided £425m towards the bill, while the rest came from ticket sales, sponsorship and other commercial sources. The report found this year's event cost 85% less to stage than the average of the previous three Games. The 2014 games featured nearly 5,000 athletes who competed in more than 17 sports. Before the 2026 Games, organisers said 500,000 tickets had been made available for sale across the programme, compared with 1.2m for Glasgow 2014. [BBC] Analysis: Glasgow 2026 was never going to have the same look or feel of Glasgow 2014 - it was never meant to. This was a stopgap Games - an event that was designed to provide life support to an organisation fighting for survival and relevancy. This impact report makes a compelling case that it was mission accomplished but questions st

item.title: Tom Brady Blurts Out a Swear Word on Live TV for the Second Time, Fan Jokes It’s Now His ‘Catchphrase’
item.description: NDZ/starmaxinc.com/Newscom/The Mega Agency Tom Brady suffered another slip of the tongue. A month after accidentally using a swear word on live TV , the seven-time Super Bowl champ , 49, blurted out the same one again while playing a trivia game with fellow retired quarterback Drew Brees on the Fox NFL Sunday broadcast on Sunday, November 1. “Drew has the most 300-yard passing games ever. Tom is second. Who’s in third?” host Curt Menefee quizzed them, per a clip posted on X . “Drew Brees,” answered Brady before realizing his mistake and uttering “Oh [expletive]!” The New England Patriots legend quickly made a face and tightly pressed his lips together when he realized his gaffe. X/Ari Meirov “ Peyton Manning is the answer,” Menefee concluded, as the other hosts laughed. “And we let you get away with one, by the way, Tom. We heard you, that’s OK.” Brady’s first error came on September 20, while reacting to a serious injury suffered by Washington Commanders player Jayden Daniels . “Another live ‘oh [expletive]’ from Brady… at this point it’s less a slip-up and more a signature catchphrase!!” one fan commented on X , while another added , “Even legends have their unfiltered moments. 😂” “Brady said what all of us been yelling at the TV all afternoon,” one fan pointed out . Others weren’t as amused. “Someone please give the guy a bar of soap,” added one , while another noted , “disgusting. i hope my kids don’t hear this.” But even more fans argued that the word itself isn’t so bad. “Yeah I think every American has heard the word [expletive] before, and the F word as well. 🙄,” wrote one. Another agreed , “Everyone’s grandma says it.” Read More From First for Sports Gabby Williams Scores $90K Bonus After Leading Golden State Valkyries to WNBA Championship Why the Milwaukee Brewers Smoked Cigarettes Before Every World Series Game: ‘Ready to Rock’ Packers’ Josh Jacobs Says His Touchdown Celebration Was Not Mocking His Domestic Violence Arrest This story Tom Brady Blurts Out a Swear Word on Live TV for the Second Time, Fan Jokes It’s Now His ‘Catchphrase’ first appeared on First for Sports . item.title: Laporta joins forces with Barcelona mayor in bid to bring 2030 World Cup final to Camp Nou
item.description: Laporta joins forces with Barcelona mayor in bid to bring 2030 World Cup final to Camp Nou Barcelona have ambitious plans for their fully renovated Spotify Camp Nou, with hosting the 2030 World Cup final high on their list of priorities. The Catalan club have already pushed for and secured permission to host the 2029 Champions League final. The ambition to host the World Cup final has now received fresh backing from the city’s political leadership and the Spanish football federation. According to SPORT , Barcelona president Joan Laporta, city mayor Jaume Collboni and Spanish Football Federation president Rafael Louzan have joined forces in pursuit of that common dream. Laporta optimistic about Camp Nou’s World Cup final ambitions Laporta, never one to mince his words, has repeatedly expressed his desire to see Barcelona’s stadium host the 2030 World Cup final. Despite facing strong competition from the Santiago Bernabeu , the Barça president has been quietly confident. “We are optimistic and hope that it happens,” the Barcelona president declared during an event featuring the World Cup trophy at city hall. Joan Laporta wants the 2030 World Cup final at the Spotify Camp Nou. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) His ambition is shared by the mayor, Collboni, who has emerged as another major supporter of the candidacy. “We would love July 21, 2030, the day of the World Cup final, to be at Camp Nou. And for Spain’s captain to lift the trophy here again,” the mayor explained. “It is the best stadium and will be the best ground in Europe. We want it to host the World Cup final, and we are working to achieve that dream.” Barcelona face competition from Madrid and Morocco The Spanish federation also welcomed Barcelona’s ambitions, but Louzan stopped short of giving his full backing to the Camp Nou. This is understandable given his position as federation president and the fact that the Santiago Bernabeu is also a realistic option for the event. “Hopefully it happens. There are possibilities,” he acknowledged, while stressing that Spain should host the final. The Camp Nou is shaping up to become one of the best stadiums in Europe. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He insisted on Spain hosting the final because Morocco has emerged as a serious competitor. The African country plans to put forward Grand Stade Hassan II as its preferred venue for the final. The 2030 World Cup is set to be co-hosted by Portugal, Spain and Morocco. However, there appears to be no real pressure from the Portuguese side. Interestingly, Morocco became a co-host of the tournament only because Ukraine could not, due to the prevailing geopolitical conditions. Spain were the original hosts alongside Morocco and are right to demand that the final be hosted there. The Camp Nou will be the biggest and most prestigious stadium in the country once renovations are complete, and it remains to be seen whether Laporta sees his dream realised.

item.title: Mid-major freshmen to know
item.description: Montverde Academy Eagles guard Dhani Miller (2) shoots the ball over Gillion Academy Lions forward Travis Tripplett Jr. (4) during the first quarter of a City of Palms Classic Signature Series game at Suncoast Credit Union Arena in Fort Myers, Fla., on Friday, Dec. 19, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co At this point, you’ve heard about Tyran Stokes, Jordan Smith Jr., Caleb Holt and many other high-major freshman who will be high impact players this season. However, they are not the only diaper dandies worth knowing about. There are some mid-major freshmen who are going to make a huge impact this year. Dhani Miller — Kent State I am not quite sure how a guy who was playing at Montverde Academy fell so under the radar, but hey, we’ll take Dhani Miller at the mid-major level. The 6-foot-2 guard averaged over 15 points a game in the EYBL Scholastic League last season and led Montverde in scoring. He is a powerful guard who is relentless getting to the basket and can finish over bigger defenders. He has shown a quick release when shooting off the dribble. I expect Miller to be one of the best players in the MAC this season. Josiah Johnson — UC Irvine Russell Turner is a defense-first coach, but his offense could be better than expected with Josiah Johnson in the mix this season. Johnson, a gifted scorer out of Southern California, will make a huge impact on the ball this season. Johnson has an extremely high basketball IQ and is great at picking his spots to attack. He doesn’t often get sped up and looks comfortable operating in the pick and roll. His passing has been on display in games I have watched, which is exciting given that he will have Olivier Rioux as a lob threat. Listen to the “Anything But Mid” Podcast: View Link Dionte Neal — UNC Greensboro I will admit, I have a bit of a soft spot for small guards. Dionte Neal is no exception. At just 5-foot-9, Neal accomplished a ton has a multi-sport athlete in high school but will now focus on basketball at UNC Greensboro. He is explosive with the ball in his hands and gets where he wants on the floor. His height is often not a weakness as defenders have a difficult time keeping up with his pace. During his senior season, Neal averaged over 35 points, four rebounds (at 5-foot-9!), eight assists and six steals. He became the first player in the history of North Carolina high school basketball to record 1,000 steals and will now try to become to hometown hero in Greensboro. Tyshawn Duncan — Louisiana I had to go with at least one big, and Tyshawn Duncan is a guy I think can come in and dominate at the mid-major level right away. Duncan is an old-school power forward or undersized center at 6-foot-8, but the way he plays makes you forget that at least height-wise, he is small for his position. I use the phrase “college-ready body” way too much, but for Duncan, it definitely applies. His game is good combo of power and finesse. item.title: Who is Joe Fagnano? The Jaguars defense to get crash course on Ravens QB
item.description: Just who in the heck is Joe Fagnano ? The Jacksonville Jaguars defense will be scrambling during a short work week to find out. Barring a fast healing process by Baltimore Ravens second-team quarterback Tyler Huntley, who left Sunday's game vs. the Buffalo Bills with a case of turf toe, and barring any moves to bring in a veteran, the Jaguars will be facing an undrafted rookie in Joe Fagnano on Nov. 5 at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore (8:15 p.m., Prime). Fagnano, seeing his first NFL action after Lamar Jackson broke his thumb on the game's first play and Huntley went down in the second quarter, completed 10 of 19 passes for 91 yards, was sacked three times and had two turnovers in the 36-10 loss on Nov. 1 that left the Ravens (4-4) stunned by how quickly their season is now on the edge. Two quarterbacks hurt in the first half is a nightmare scenario. But Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he doesn't buy into bad luck or jinxes. “That would be the self-pity version. I don't really believe in that," he said. "Things happen. It's [about] how you respond. There's no testimony without a test. So, we'll do everything in our power to keep rolling, to keep this thing going, to get it back on the right side, again with whatever that looks like, and whoever that's playing. If it's Joe [Fagnano], we have a lot of belief in Joe.” By the way, it's pronounced "Fin-YAWN-oh." Will the backup QB jinx hit the Jaguars? Minter is now faced with a short week and possibly having to put the ball in the hands of a former UConn star who also played three years at Maine, the alma mater of Jaguars coach Liam Coen . "I thought Joe came in, to his credit, not really getting a lot of reps in preparation, hung in there [and] did some good stuff," Minter said. "It's a short week. It's an opportunity again to stick together, to work together, come together." Since the Jaguars have had a disturbing habit in the past of losing to backup quarterbacks (Davis Mills, Jake Browning, Joe Flacco with two teams, Malik Willis to name a few recent examples), it's doubtful Coen and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will allow the defense to take Fagnano, or Huntley, if he's able to play, lightly. "It's really on us to play our defense better than they play their offense," Jaguars linebacker Foye Oluokun said on Nov. 2 during a virtual news conference with the media, 18 hours after the Jags (5-2) put the finishing touches on a 42-7 victory over the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium and 82 hours before they will play the Ravens. "That's what we're going to focus on this week. I don't want to focus into that backup quarterback stuff. Anybody who's in the NFL is capable enough." While the Jaguars have struggled with backups (Mills is 3-1 as a starter, Flacco is 2-0, beating the Jaguars with the Browns and the Colts after his lengthy career in Baltimore, and Browning is 2-0), Fagnano is a different case. item.title: Hornets Have Run Out Of Reasons To Play Sion James
item.description: Charlotte Hornets guard Sion James (4) drives to the basket as Washington Wizards forward Khris Middleton (22) defends in the first half in an NBA Cup game at Capital One Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Charlotte Hornets offense has struggled in a variety of ways without Kon Knueppel and Coby White — dropping their last three games. One of the Hornets’ biggest storylines was Naz Reid getting benched after one half, but eyes have turned to Sion James ‘ play as a starter. James has been forced into a starter role with Knueppel and White sidelined with injuries. The spot starts have gone haywire, and Hornets fans are noticing. The Shooting Slump Has Been Backbreaking To The Hornets’ Offense Frankly, James has been one of the worst shooters in the NBA to start the regular season. He is averaging 3.7 points per game on 22/15/75 shooting splits. Through seven games, James is 9-for-41 from the field and 5-for-33 from three. It’s gone beyond “bad shooting.” Right now, he’s arguably the league’s least efficient scorer. Of every player averaging 15-plus minutes, James ranks dead last in true shooting percentage (30.4). Sion James blows the open reverse layup in the clutch Via: https://t.co/kRD3AN3Nbu pic.twitter.com/EepNPkkMgH — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 1, 2026 Is it truly a slump or pure regression from the second-year guard? It’s not like James is taking bad shots. For example, over 58 percent of his three-point attempts have been wide-open shots. The problem: he’s just not converting them. Last year with the Hornets, James was called upon as a strong 3-and-D player off the bench — and he played well. With more pressure mounting on him as a starter due to injuries to Knueppel and White, his confidence has slowly faded. His shots aren’t falling right now, and Charles Lee needs to make a change to the starting lineup to make it function more efficiently. Charles Lee Still Believes In Sion James Despite Struggles Charlotte Hornets head coach Charles Lee argues with the officials during their game against the Detroit Pistons in the second quarter at Little Caesars Arena. Photo Credit: Lon Horwedel, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect You are doing something right if your head coach speaks highly of you after a dreadful start. Lee was asked by Hornets Insider Rod Boone why James is starting and what his thoughts are about his struggles missing open shots: “[James ‘] competitive spirit becomes contagious with our whole group,” Lee explained. Being one of the top 10 defenses in the NBA is a huge accomplishment for our group right now, despite being undermanned. I think he’s a big part of why we’ve been able to trend positively in our turnover percentages… he’s gotten some good looks, and we all go through some shooting slumps, but I love what he’s given us on both ends of the floor.” Why is Charles Lee starting Sion James, and what are his thoughts on Sion’s struggles to hit open shots? item.title: Cowboys ‘made a mistake’ not hiring ex-Jets coach as defensive coordinator
item.description: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones may not be leaning towards a mid-season coaching change, but he “made a mistake” not hiring former Jets and Bills head coach Rex Ryan as his defensive coordinator, Stephen A. Smith says. Smith’s comments on First Take came one day after the Cowboys blew a 14-point second-half lead and lost at home to the Arizona Cardinals, 33-30, in overtime on Sunday. The Cowboys (3-5) allowed 30 points in the second half and overtime. The Cowboys had a 202-0-1 record with a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter, per ESPN. Smith, a noted Cowboys critic, called it a “pathetic” performance and said the “Cowboys are trash,” while adding that Jones should have hired Ryan instead of the embattled Christian Parker. “Jerry Jones made a mistake by not going and getting Rex Ryan to be his defensive coordinator,” Smith said. “You need somebody fiery, you need somebody that’s gonna hold cats accountable, you need somebody that’s gonna make people recognize that their jobs are on the line if they don’t go out there and produce... “The losses don’t hurt enough because life is real comfortable in Big D.” Former Cowboys star Michael Irvin said that Parker, whose team has allowed 20+ points in 15 straight games, “is totally overwhelmed.” “Right now, it is bad,” Irvin said. “There is no getting around that, and snatching defeat from the jaws of victory is a new pain and a new low.” MORE BY ADAM ZAGORIA Yankees will ‘be involved’ in market for Japanese slugger Nov. 2, 2026, 11:58 a.m. Yankees star shows out with daughter to support wife in NYC Marathon Nov. 2, 2026, 8:43 a.m. Former NFL QB Dan Orlovsky said “the Cowboys need to make a change somewhere within their football team. They’re 3-5.” That change apparently won’t include Jones firing Brian Schottenheimer in the middle of the season despite his 10-14 record with the Cowboys. “I made a change, and I don’t want to mention it because I’m not proud of it,” Jones told reporters after the loss. “But I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season, and I don’t see that here at all.” Read the original article on NJ.com . item.title: How Mercedes can clinch F1 Constructors’ Championship in Brazil
item.description: (Photo by Jayce Illman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kimi Antonelli made history in Sunday’s Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest Drivers’ Champion in the history of the sport. Now he and the rest of Mercedes can turn their eyes to another prize, the Constructors’ Championship. Mercedes had a narrow path to clinching the Constructors’ title last Sunday in Mexico, but now the math is a little easier for them starting with next weekend’s São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos. Here is how the Silver Arrows can clinch the team’s first Constructors’ Championship since 2021 in Brazil. How Mercedes can clinch in São Paulo Thanks to Antonelli’s third-place finish in Mexico City, and a sixth-place finish from George Russell, Mercedes enters the São Paulo Grand Prix with 630 points, giving the team a commanding 126-point lead over Ferrari with four race weekends remaining, including the upcoming São Paulo Grand Prix: Mercedes: 630 points Ferrari: 504 points Ferrari is the only team with a mathematical chance to catch Mercedes in the standings. Given that each of the remaining races follows the standard Grand Prix format (and does not include an F1 Sprint race) the maximum points available to a team each weekend is 43: 25 points for a win, and 18 points for a second-place finish. That means that to clinch the Constructors’ Championship, Mercedes needs to leave the São Paulo Grand Prix with at least a 129-point lead. After Brazil, only three races will remain, offering a maximum of 129 points. Mercedes has already clinched the “countback” tiebreaker over Ferrari, as the Silver Arrows have won 12 races, compared to two for Ferrari, so even if the Scuderia win every remaining race, Mercedes will have more wins. So if the teams finish level on points, the number of wins serves as the first tiebreaker, and Mercedes has clinched that countback tiebreaker. So how can Mercedes reach that 129-point advantage, and clinch the title in Mexico City? They need to extend the current 126-point lead by just three points. That would push their advantage to 129 points, mathematically eliminating Ferrari from contention. How can they clinch? The first is with a one-two finish in Brazil. If either Antonelli or Russell wins the São Paulo Grand Prix and the other driver finishes second, that would give Mercedes 43 points, moving their season total to 673. Even if Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton combine to finish third and fourth, that would give Ferrari 27 points, bringing their total to 531. And the gap between the two teams would be 142 points, more than enough for Mercedes to clinch. The Silver Arrows can also clinch with a P1-P3 combination. That would give Mercedes 40 points, and move their season total to 670. Then even if Ferrari finish second and fourth, their total would increase to 534 points, a gap of 136 points, more than enough to lock up the title for Mercedes. item.title: Former Munday star L.J. Collier delivers late in Cardinals' win over Cowboys
item.description: Former Munday High School standout L.J. Collier made his presence felt when the Arizona Cardinals needed it most Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys . Collier finished with three tackles, a sack, a tackle for loss, two quarterback hits and two pass breakups as Arizona rallied for a 33-30 overtime victory at AT&T Stadium. His biggest plays came late, too. More: VOTE NOW | Vote for the Week 10 Texoma boys Athlete of the Week More: See the Week 11 Texoma high school football schedule More: UIL volleyball playoffs: Area-round matchups for Texoma teams With Dallas trying to protect its lead in the fourth quarter, Collier knocked down a Dak Prescott pass on third-and-11 with 3:58 remaining. He got to Prescott again less than two minutes later, dropping the Cowboys quarterback for a 6-yard sack — his first of the 2026 season — with 2:09 remaining. Dallas received the ball first in overtime, and Collier knocked down another Prescott pass during a possession that ended with the Cowboys punting. Arizona took advantage, driving into position for Chad Ryland's 42-yard field goal to complete the comeback. It was a strong response from Collier after a costly mistake earlier in the fourth quarter. He was flagged for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after the Cardinals appeared to have stopped Dallas on third down. The penalty extended the Cowboys' possession, which eventually produced a field goal and gave Dallas a 27-17 lead. Collier responded by becoming one of Arizona's most disruptive defenders down the stretch. The Cardinals (3-5) trailed 17-3 in the third quarter before rallying behind backup quarterback Gardner Minshew, who threw three touchdown passes after replacing Jacoby Brissett. Arizona tied the game on Minshew's 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with six seconds remaining before winning in overtime. Collier, a 2014 Munday graduate, is in his eighth NFL season. The former TCU defensive lineman was selected by Seattle in the first round of the 2019 NFL Draft before eventually joining Arizona. This article originally appeared on Wichita Falls Times Record News: Former Munday star L.J. Collier delivers late in Cardinals' win over Cowboys

item.title: Stock Up, Stock Down: Indiana Feels Inevitable, Ohio State Is Vulnerable, Nebraska Is Nebraska
item.description: Nebraska’s head coach Matt Rhule looks on during the second quarter in the game against Michigan State on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co STOCK UP Indiana’s Grit And/Or Luck Indiana sits at 8-1 and has No. 18 USC, @Washington, and Purdue left on the schedule. More likely than not, the Hoosiers will finish 10-2 and make the CFP. That is quite the accomplishment considering that Indiana might be one of the few programs that has made the 12-team CFP field in all three seasons. The only other programs that could potentially do it are Georgia (likely), Ohio State (50/50?), and Oregon (still technically alive, but it’s like a 5% chance). That level of consistency shouldn’t be overlooked, especially when you consider how the Hoosiers have navigated through this season. Other than the Rutgers game which was a 47-15 shellacking, Indiana has been in dogfight after dogfight. Northwestern was a 22-20 game in the 4th quarter. They trailed Nebraska 17-6 in the 4th quarter. They needed overtime to beat Michigan, and then needed a 60-yard field goal and OT to beat Minnesota. INDIANA DRILLS THEIR OWN 60-YARD FIELD GOAL TO TIE IT 🚨 pic.twitter.com/qnLowRv1TH — CFB Kings (@CFBKings) October 31, 2026 I think Indiana deserves all the credit in the world because good teams find ways to win football games and man have they found ways to win football games. But as a Penn State fan who has seemingly been on the other end of so many unlucky moments the last few years — including one toe-tap catch against the Hoosiers — I just imagine how different this season looks if these 50/50 games aren’t going their way. Lincoln Riley, I Think? Last week, I basically wrote the obituary for Lincoln Riley’s tenure at USC, and what happens next? The Trojans beat Ohio State at home in rather convincing fashion. Sure, the Buckeyes did not have Julian Sayin and were starting a true freshman three-star quarterback instead, but beating Ohio State is *always* a big deal and it rightly should be for Riley. I suppose this saves his job? Maybe? The Trojans still have a road trip to Indiana in two weeks and wrap up the season with UCLA so a 9-3 finish is still probably the most likely outcome, but with college football going the way it’s gone, it’s difficult to feel confident about any one game between semi-equal teams. Personally, I am going to do my best moving forward to not write obituaries for coaches, teams, programs, etc. in the middle of the season. There’s just too much chaos week-to-week that the vibes change with one performance. It’s truly NFL-like in that aspect. item.title: Five storylines to watch for 2026-27 Ohio State women’s basketball season
item.description: The wait is over. Ohio State women’s basketball returns to the court Monday to start the 2026-27 season. While a matchup against the University of Illinois Chicago is not the brightest beginning to the new campaign, and might not be too close after the first few minutes, it is a basketball game that counts. Head coach Kevin McGuff’s team has 31 regular season games ahead of them. Before any basketball gets dribbled though, there are already storylines to watch as the four-month regular season gets underway. Out of the Second Round There are no guarantees that the Buckeyes will make the NCAA Tournament come March, but barring any spectacular collapse, there will likely be postseason basketball for Ohio State. With that said, the Second Round of March Madness is not too popular with fans of the Scarlet and Gray. It has been three consecutive seasons of the Buckeyes hosting NCAA Basketball, only to lose in the second game of the first weekend. While powerhouse names in college basketball like the Duke Blue Devils, Tennessee Volunteers and Notre Dame Fighting Irish are respectable defeats, not as the favorite with an apparent home court advantage. Now, the normal athlete interview about a situation so far away from November elicits an expected theme or not thinking about that, focusing on the first game and doing all they can to make it that far in the first place. Not for Ohio State. It is the elephant in the room. “Just like getting out the Schott, the biggest emphasis for me this year. The rest I don’t really care about. The individual goals, I will do whatever it takes to get us out the Schott,” guard Kennedy Cambridge told reporters. Should the Buckeyes continue their upward trajectory that the young group of underclassmen showed last season, hosting a fifth season in a row is a low bar. The Cambridge Sisters For the third season in a row, guards Kennedy and Jaloni Cambridge chose Ohio State to continue their history of competing together. After this season, only a trip to the professionals for both players and a friendly general manager would bring the duo back. That means the end of the season will come with more emotion for the pair of standout guards, but it also means a final season of watching two standout guards play basketball alongside one another. The pair of Cambridges now hold program records on both sides of the ball. Jaloni Cambridge fulfilled the promise that came with being Ohio State highest ranked freshman recruit (No. 2 overall). Kennedy Cambridge, whose transfer from the Kentucky Wildcats to the Buckeyes prior to the 23-24 season was a strong catalyst in securing Jaloni’s commitment, took time to get into the starting lineup but smashed the Scarlet and Gray’s single season steals record and had over 100 takeaways for only the second time in Ohio State’s history. item.title: Four-star QB Hunter Fujikawa has committed to Stanford, breaks down why he chose the Cardinal
item.description: Mililani (Hawaii) junior quarterback Hunter Fujikawa has committed to Stanford and broke down why he chose the Cardinal. Stanford picked up their first commitment in the ’28 class and it’s a big one. Fujikawa is one of the top quarterbacks in the country and checks in as the No. 180 player nationally in the Rivals Industry Rankings, an equally weighted average that utilizes all three major recruiting services. Stanford was always on the short list with Fujikawa but we never saw them as the leader in the race. Early on, Oregon and Washington had some buzz and an offer from Michigan made a big impact. He visited UCLA two weeks ago and the Bruins were trending and Ole Miss has been on his short list from the beginning. Everything changed for Fujikawa after he visited the Farm last weekend and saw the Cardinal beat NC State. He said the visit exceeded all expectations and the talented signal caller decided to pull the trigger just a few days later. “Stanford really was the best of both worlds,” Fujikawa said. “It’s more than just football, it’s a chance to get a world-class education as well and the quarterback development is really big there. I’m going to have a chance to learn under some really good coaches and that was big for me. “Having the opportunity to learn from coaches with NFL experience and someone like Andrew Luck, who was the No. 1 overall pick and is still really involved with the program. The coaches really believe in me there and made a point to let me know that. They made it clear that they see me as a big part of the future of the program and I love the vision they have for me and the future of the program.” A special touch on his visit was a FaceTime call with Hawaii prep legend and former Oregon Heisman Trophy winner Marcus Mariota. Mariota is revered by young and old athletes alike from Hawaii, especially quarterbacks. “That was a huge highlight for sure,” Fujikawa said. “Marcus FaceTimed Coach Pritchard while I was meeting with him, and I got to talk to him over the phone and that was really special. “He’s a great quarterback, and I’ve looked up to him since I was young. Hearing him talk about how Coach Pritchard helped him rediscover his love for football made the visit even more meaningful.” Fujikawa said the offense and scheme fit was another huge plus for the Cardinal. “I love the offense,” Fujikawa said. “They broke down clips from my film and put them side by side with clips from their offense to show how similar they are. They run an NFL-style offense, which is exactly what I’m looking for. Just looking at what a great fit it is for me, along with the opportunity to develop as a quarterback, I knew this was the right move for me.”

item.title: Los Angeles Chargers are the latest NFL primetime albatross, unless flex scheduling saves us all
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Few would’ve guessed that we’d get to the month of November and the Los Angeles Chargers would still be sitting with a winless record. Even fewer would’ve believed that knowing that Justin Herbert has started every game. But here we are. The Chargers are 0-7 after their latest loss to the cross-town rival Rams, and any hope for a turnaround seems to be far in the rearview. Instead, questions about Herbert, head coach Jim Harbaugh, and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel are the only things making the Chargers a relevant national storyline. With three Chargers primetime games on the horizon, however, it’ll be incumbent upon the NFL to find some alternatives to the sputtering Bolts, otherwise fans will be subjected to some rather low-stakes football in some of the biggest windows of the season. Unfortunately, the first Chargers primetime game cannot be flexed at all. ESPN’s Monday Night Football in Week 10 features the Chargers and the Baltimore Ravens, a team that is currently down to its third-string quarterback and sitting in last place in the AFC North. But per the NFL’s flex scheduling rules, games cannot be flexed out of Monday Night Football until Week 12, meaning there’s nothing the league or ESPN can do to improve the matchup two weeks from now. Things will get interesting in Week 12 and Week 15, however. The Chargers are scheduled to headline Sunday Night Football in Week 12 against the New England Patriots, a game that can be flexed under the league’s flex scheduling procedures. However, that week is particularly tricky to flex because it is the week of Thanksgiving. The NFL already has six other standalone games scheduled that week: one on Thanksgiving Eve, three on Thanksgiving, one on Black Friday, and one on Monday Night Football . That leaves very few quality games in the Sunday afternoon slate that would be available to flex the Chargers out of primetime. The best options would likely be Saints-Bengals, Falcons-Vikings, or Raiders-Browns; none of which really scream “worthy of primetime placement.” It’ll be interesting to see whether the NFL chooses to utilize a flex here. Week 15 poses another interesting scenario. The Chargers are scheduled to play the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday Night Football . The NFL can flex TNF games after Week 13, but must give a 21-day notice as opposed to the normal six- or 12-day notice the league is usually afforded (depending on which package and how late in the year the flex is happening). Only once in the league’s history has the NFL flexed a Thursday game; in 2024 to swap out Browns-Bengals for Broncos-Chargers. It’s unclear if 49ers-Chargers would meet the threshold for a Thursday flex, considering the 49ers figure to be Super Bowl contenders and that game will likely have playoff implications for them. So despite the Chargers sporting an 0-7 record heading into Week 9, it’s quite possible the team is featured in three primetime slots the remainder of the season.

item.title: Stefon Diggs Says His Assault Accuser Tried to Steal His Clothes—and Insists His ‘Caught Stealing’ Post Was True
item.description: Image Credit: All-Pro Reels - Flickr, CC BY-SA 2.0/Wiki Commons. Stefon Diggs is standing by the social media post accusing Christopher Blake Griffith of stealing from him. In a filing reported by TMZ on October 30, the receiver argued that his comments were true and should not expose him to defamation liability. "Lying on my name because he got caught stealing," the post read. Griffith says the remarks targeted him and damaged his reputation. He disputes Diggs's accusation that he tried to take clothing from the football player's home. Diggs brought the original defamation lawsuit in Maryland state court in October 2025, accusing Griffith of spreading fabricated allegations. Griffith subsequently filed counterclaims against him. The latest response follows an argument Diggs made in August, when he opposed Griffith's effort to expand those counterclaims. He maintained then, too, that the disputed statement was truthful. Griffith alleges that Diggs gave him candy containing an intoxicating substance at his home and sexually assaulted him. His attorney, Jacob Lebowitz, described the allegation as sexual battery in an interview with the station. Diggs denies drugging Griffith or making the alleged advances. In a July 17 interview with TMZ, Griffith rejected suggestions that his case was a financial shakedown. He said he had not demanded a specific dollar amount and wanted accountability for what he says happened to him. Diggs's Lawyer Disputes the Claim That He Arranged an Attack Griffith also alleges that Diggs arranged for several men, including his brother Darez, to attack him at his Los Angeles apartment building about a week later. Diggs's attorney, Mitch Schuster, denied that his client organized, facilitated or participated in the incident in a statement to Us Weekly on July 22. Schuster said that interpretation misrepresented communications Diggs had not participated in. He also said Diggs routinely paid travel and accommodation expenses for friends and relatives without directing their activities. Griffith separately settled a civil lawsuit involving Darez and a Los Angeles apartment complex in July. item.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
item.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists have found that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS was built from tiny grains of ice mixed with dust that are quite different from the solar system’s comets. These ice grains do, however, bear striking similarities to some icy bodies located at the edge of the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, so-called trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs). 3I/ATLAS was discovered entering the solar system in the summer of 2025. It was only the third object found entering the solar system from farther afield in the Milky Way after 1I/'Oumuamua , seen in 2017, and 2I/Borisov , detected in 2019. This meant the interstellar comet offered a rare chance to glimpse the conditions under which such bodies form in other star systems. Thus, the JWST was quickly on the trail of 3I/ATLAS. "We designed [JWST] to be ready the moment an active interstellar comet was found and to follow it over time," Martin Cordiner of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Catholic University of America said in a statement . Cordiner leads the JWST program to study objects such as 3I/ATLAS, and he is a co-author on a new research paper describing some of the findings. The unclear origins of 3I/ATLAS Researchers know that 3I/ATLAS wasn't born in the solar system, but nobody knows around which star 3I/ATLAS formed. What scientists are more sure of is the fact that this interstellar comet was produced within a planet-forming disk of gas and dust around a young star, possibly as long ago as 10 to 12 billion years . That's over twice the age of our solar system. It was then ejected from its home system somehow and left to wander interstellar space before encountering our solar system. Like the familiar comets in our solar system, 3I/ATLAS is composed of grains of ice less than a micron – a millionth of a meter – in size. When the surface of the comet is warmed by the sun , gas erupts outwards, carrying ice grains into the cloud of ice and dust surrounding the comet, its coma, and its tail, where JWST can detect them. When viewed spectroscopically, the water-ice in comets native to our solar system creates a strong absorption line in a comet’s spectrum at a wavelength of three microns, as well as less-prominent absorption lines at 1.5 and two microns. Comparison between ice in the interstellar invader comet 3I/Atlas and icy bodies in our solar system. (Image credit: SwRI/Silvia Protopapa/NASA/ESA/CSA JWST) Yet when the JWST’s Near-Infrared spectrograph ( NIRSpec ) instrument viewed 3I/ATLAS three times between August 2025, before its closest approach to the sun, and after closest approach in April 2026, scientists found the 1.5- and two micron absorption lines were missing, though the three-micron line remained strong. "That combination was a puzzle," research lead author Silvia Protopapa of the South-west Research Institute said. item.title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ win over the Dolphins
item.description: Allow me to be the first to welcome everyone to the best time of the year! 3:30 p.m. sunsets and constant darkness, here we come! It’s wild how I used to actually enjoy the first night of Daylight Savings Time starting, or ending, or whichever one this one is. You’re out at the bars, they’re about to close…and then all of a sudden, you get an extra hour to make bad decisions. But I’ve aged out of all that, alas, so now I’m taking up the mantle of the crotchety middle-aged man who likes to complain about everything. At least I’m not complaining about a Patriots loss, though, as New England took care of business to the tune of a 24-19 victory to move ahead to 5-3, 3-0 in the AFC East . I had absolutely no idea what to expect coming into this game. Sure, the Fins stink, but nothing is as it seems when the Patriots head down to Miami. Compound that with rainy conditions, an oddly-positioned 4:25 slot for a game that certainly didn’t deserve a late window, and an absolutely decimated Patriots team, and this just seemed to have all the makings of a trap game. And for the first half, that’s exactly what seemed to be happening. New England couldn’t move the ball at all, the defense was oddly off, and the whole game just seemed like holiday commercials before Halloween even hits; nobody wants to see that. But something happened in that locker room at halftime, because the Patriots came out and scored on three consecutive drives to open this one up. But I’m getting ahead of myself. I have a few more complaints to lodge before I break this game down in earnest. As the Patriots played in the late window for the first time this year, I watched the 1 p.m. games for the first time all season. And I wish I was saying differently, but the NFL is becoming completely unwatchable. The games have zero flow to them. The officiating somehow seems to be getting worse every year as opposed to better, and everyone just kind of stinks. As a product, it has been trending in the wrong direction for years now, and I’m starting to wonder when I’m going to just stop watching altogether. Probably when the NFL inevitably starts offering Tuesday Night Football, Wednesday Night Football, and Friday Night Football to completely oversaturate the market. Children would love to eat chocolate and candy with every meal, but normal adults don’t allow that. You need to limit things. OK, enough of that. Sorry to open on a downer. I just used to love the NFL so damn much, and it’s losing me, and that makes me sad. On the plus side, the horrendous officiating and terrible refs blessed us with what might be the most spectacular display of infathomable incompetence we’re going to see this year. On New England’s second possession of the third quarter, Drake Maye hit Kyle Williams for what turned out to be a 43-yard touchdown. Williams caught the ball at the five-yard line, took four or five steps, crossed the goal line, then his knee hit the ball and came loose. The goal-line referee threw a blu

item.title: 'Just next level': Jayson Tatum shares what has blown him away about Paul George this season
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Jayson Tatum and Paul George have formed quite the partnership since joining forces with the Boston Celtics. On Sunday night, the Celtics secured a 108-97 win against the Orlando Magic on the road, and Tatum showed why he is their star player once again. However, George produced a number of incredible moments, and his fellow forward heaped praise on him after the game. Jayson Tatum says Paul George’s game awareness is ‘just next level’ Paul George has been in the NBA for 17 years now and has played with some big players. The veteran may not have won a championship ring yet, but he is viewed by many as an incredible player, and his performances lately speak for themselves. Against the Magic, George scored 17 points and recorded six rebounds, eight assists, two steals and two blocks during his 33 minutes on the floor. That seems to have impressed Tatum, who heaped praise on him after the game. He said on NBC Sports Boston : “It (the chemistry) is great. We continue to get better. “He hit some unbelievable shots. His awareness on the defensive end and his activity with his hands is just next level. He always has awareness with the ball and deflections. “He makes it easier on the rest of us, even this late in his career.” Tatum had formed a stunning partnership with Jaylen Brown when they were together in Boston, so George had some big shoes to fill. However, so far, he is doing what he is expected to do, which is good news for Celtics fans and their ambitions for the season. item.description: President Bola Tinubu has concluded his visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed the lesser Hajj, known as Umrah, and entered the Holy Kaaba to offer prayers. Tinubu disclosed this in a statement following the visit, expressing gratitude to Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the privilege. The President also appreciated the Saudi leadership for its hospitality and support, describing the gesture as a reflection of the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and the Kingdom. He said he used the opportunity to pray for peace, unity and prosperity in Nigeria. “I have concluded my visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where, together with members of my delegation, I had the rare honour of entering the Holy Kaaba to pray, and of performing Umrah. “I am deeply grateful to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and to Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for extending this privilege to us, and for their gracious hospitality and brotherly care. It reflects the enduring bonds of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “In those sacred moments, I prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for our dear nation and for all Nigerians,” He wrote. The post Tinubu concludes Saudi Arabia visit, says he prayed for Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sokoto SSANU begins warning strike over unpaid entitlements
item.description: ….Union threatens indefinite shutdown if demands remain unmet By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Sokoto State University (SSU) chapter, has commenced a five-working-day warning strike over outstanding staff entitlements, threatening an indefinite shutdown if the dispute with the Sokoto State Government is not resolved. The union said the industrial action followed the expiration of a 14-working-day ultimatum issued to the state government over its demands. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Ismail Bala Muhammed, and Secretary, Mansur Ahmad, SSANU said the strike was triggered by the government’s failure to approve and implement the outstanding entitlements despite repeated engagements. The association said it initially submitted its demands through the appropriate channels before forwarding a comprehensive document on July 28, 2026, following the agreement between the Federal Government and the union on the 35 per cent Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA). It said it subsequently made several verbal and written appeals, including visits to the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry and the Deputy Governor, in a bid to secure an amicable settlement. Following the engagements, the state government constituted a committee comprising the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary, the Deputy Accountant-General and Professor Mustapha Aliyu to engage representatives of SSANU, the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT) and the Non-Academic Staff Union (NASU) from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education. At a meeting on October 9, the government communicated its position on the outstanding claims. However, SSANU said the response failed to address its members’ major concerns. According to the union, the government rejected payment of arrears arising from the 25 per cent salary increment, proposed implementing CONTTA from January 2027 subject to budgetary provision, and maintained that annual salary increments had already been implemented. Dissatisfied with the outcome, SSANU said it convened an emergency congress on October 13, where members resolved to issue a 14-working-day ultimatum to the government. The union warned that failure to meet its demands would trigger a five-day warning strike and potentially an indefinite industrial action. It, however, temporarily suspended the planned announcement of the strike after the Permanent Secretary scheduled a meeting with representatives of SSANU from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education on October 14. At the meeting, the Permanent Secretary reportedly disclosed that the governor had directed the unions to resubmit their demands, separating existing claims from new ones and indicating their respective financial implications. The unions were also asked to distinguish between demands with lower and higher financial implications. Following deliberatio

item.title: NASS Considering Proposal To Create 74 Seats For Women, Says Bamidele
item.description: Leader of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, on Monday disclosed that the National Assembly Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) had proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives Bamidele, also Vice Chairman, Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, further revealed that the committee had proposed three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. He made this disclosure at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter on Monday, noting that the proposals were designed to deepen the inclusion of women in the country’s politics and governance process. A file photo of Senator Opeyemi Bamidele Ekiti FIDA, chaired by Mrs. Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, organised the programme with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” Bamidele attended the programme alongside the Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Information and National Orientation, Steve Fatoba, and Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, among others. “A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly,” Bamidele said. He further explained the centerpiece of the legislative initiative, which, according to him, was designed to create special seats for women at the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly under the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution. He added that the legislative initiative “is the fruit of extensive consultation and consensus-building. “It is why we commenced the constitutional amendment process early, ensuring that this is not a rushed, haphazard endeavour but a deliberate, inclusive, and thorough reform. “The proposal, as it stands, is meticulous in its design. It seeks to add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 seats in the House of Representatives. This suggests that if finally approved, each state of the federation, including FCT, will have one additional seat in each of the Houses of the National Assembly,” he added. Bamidele further revealed that the constitution review committee “has already proposed three additional seats for each state House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. “This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review. This is a sunset clause designed to ensure sustainability and to allow for the organic development of a more inclusive political culture,” the senator said. “We are actively and strategically engaging with the State Houses of Assembly, as their concurrence is a constitutional sine

item.title: Thieves pilfer environment variables from Trigger AI workflow tool
item.description: If you're a customer of cloud-hosted AI workflow platform Trigger.dev, take heed, because your environment variables may have been exposed in a security incident disclosed on Sunday. Trigger offered little explanation in its Sunday security incident report , noting that its investigation had identified “exposure across a subset of organizations” and that an attacker had gained unauthorized access to environment variables belonging to those organizations. Whatever exploit was used to gain access has been blocked, the company added, and affected customers have been notified of steps they need to take to prevent further security problems. We likely don't have to tell The Reg readers how important environment variables are in SaaS and cloud services like Trigger. If compromised environment variables contain sensitive credentials, an attacker could basically end up with the keys to the kingdom, potentially gaining access to connected services and digital infrastructure. For those unfamiliar with Trigger.dev, it’s a platform for building AI agents and workflows in TypeScript, but here’s the kicker: Trigger advertises itself as a durable execution platform that handles pesky things like retries, scaling, and keeping long-running tasks going through crashes and redeployments, while providing tools to monitor what those tasks are doing. Trigger, the company’s site notes, can be used to “build durable AI agents that survive refreshes, redeploys, and crashes,” and is ideal for “long-running tasks with retries, queues, AI observability and elastic scaling.” In short, companies running their AI on Trigger probably want it to keep running, which makes stolen environment variables all the more dangerous. Elastic scaling, automated retries, and, as Trigger notes, the ability to run lots of concurrent operations without timeouts could compound the consequences of compromised API keys, depending on what those credentials allow an attacker to access. An attacker with stolen credentials could potentially interfere with a customer's connected services or workflows. Additionally, Trigger recently added webhooks to its offering, supporting services like Stripe, Supabase, and Slack, potentially expanding the range of integrations that could be affected if their credentials were exposed. This could be pretty bad for anyone affected. Trigger has some fairly high-profile customers, with companies like fashion brand Emporio Armani, Pentagon-supporting AI acquisitions platform GovSignals, SaaS calendar platform Cal.com, and others all listed on the company’s site. Trigger has not publicly identified which organizations were affected by the intrusion. We reached out to Trigger, which declined to provide any additional information on the incident. A company spokesperson instead told us to wait for a full incident report to learn more. Luckily for Trigger customers and those concerned about SaaS security now that AI is regularly coming up with new vulnerabilities in commonly us

item.title: Otti: Abia won’t celebrate thieves, drug barons again
item.description: …Governor honours Emeritus Professor Oluikpe at 90 By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said his administration is working to dismantle what he described as a culture of celebrating thieves, fraudsters, drug barons and other questionable characters, insisting that public recognition should be reserved for people of integrity and genuine accomplishments. Otti spoke at the 90th birthday celebration of Emeritus Professor Benson Oluikpe in Umuahia, where he said his administration was institutionalising the celebration of excellence to inspire younger generations to pursue worthy achievements. “We want to depart from that inherited culture. It’s not our culture. Culture of celebrating thieves. Culture of celebrating 419-ers. Culture of celebrating drug barons. Culture of celebrating bandits. That’s not our culture. That’s not how we grew up,” the governor said. He faulted the practice of honouring outstanding individuals only after their death, when they could no longer enjoy the recognition, saying achievers should be celebrated while alive. According to him, recognising people for their contributions would encourage others, particularly young people, to aspire to excellence. Otti cited the recent celebration of five Abia schoolchildren who emerged champions at an international competition in Qatar, saying his administration was determined to make excellence, rather than questionable wealth and influence, the basis for public recognition. The governor also used a personal experience to illustrate the importance of accountability, recalling how his father questioned him in 1989 over the source of the N100 he sent home while working at Citibank. He said he had earned the money through extra work and daily allowances, but his father insisted on knowing how he legitimately made it. “That’s how I was brought up. You needed to give account. But these days, people don’t ask questions. We need to go back to that time when we would ask questions. Ask your children questions. Let them give account,” he said. Otti maintained that people’s values, rather than the times, had changed, citing his son’s decision to provide receipts and explanations for money he had saved towards buying a house in the United States. Earlier, Oluikpe expressed gratitude for the honour and prayed for God’s blessings on the governor. “You have honoured me; may God honour you,” the nonagenarian said. The professor, who disclosed that he first met Otti in 2013 when the governor was still a banker, described him as a humble man endowed with wisdom. He said the impression he formed of Otti during their first encounter influenced his subsequent support for the governor’s political ambition. Recounting how Otti once stood up to return an award to him at a public function, Oluikpe said the gesture demonstrated a humility that had remained consistent in the governor’s public life. He also described Otti’s electoral setback in 2015 as a divine postponement of his political

item.title: 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -A political group,Niger Delta Youth Movement, NDYM, has warned an aide to Governor Hope Uzodinma,Mr. Collins Opurozor,to stop attacking the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory,FCT, Nyesom Wike over the senatorial tussle between the Governor and Owelle Rochas Okorocha. The group also urged Opurozor not to use the disagreement between the two APC Chieftains to create hostility between the South East zone and Wike. The group alleged that Opurozor has been attempting to undermine Wike through inflammatory political remarks. The Movement declared that it would not continue to watch Opurozor attack the FCT Minister without consequences and urged him to exercise restraint and desist from using media interviews to settle political scores. In a statement by its Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jeffery Nwali, NDYM condemned Opurozor’s comments on a national television where he accused Wike of attempting to turn the South East into his personal political fiefdom by allegedly encouraging the emergence of weak leaders in the region to preserve his political influence. Describing the comments as reckless and provocative,the group,however, insisted that Wike’s political engagements should not be misrepresented as an attack on Igbo interests. The statement read;”We condemn the attempt by Collins Opurozor to drag the FCT Minister into Imo State’s political disputes, particularly following the Federal High Court judgment concerning Governor Uzodinma’s APC senatorial candidacy in Imo West senatorial zone. “Disagreements between Uzodinma and other political actors in Imo State should not be allowed to create unnecessary hostility between the South East and the FCT Minister. “During the television interview, Opurozor strongly criticized the judgment, dismissed Senator Samuel Anyanwu over what he described as his lack of grassroots support in Imo State, and berated the administration of former Governor Rochas Okorocha as too disgraceful to be remembered. “He also accused Wike of undermining Igbo political interests by allegedly supporting political figures opposed to Uzodinma. “Collins Opurozor is a young political aide who over- rates his intelligence and mistakes verbal aggression for political sophistication. Political disagreements should not become excuses to denigrate established political leaders.” The post 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria targets wider access to West African markets
item.description: … FG urges businesses to exploit ECOWAS trade scheme By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja LOKOJA — The Federal Government has urged Nigerian manufacturers, farmers and entrepreneurs to take advantage of the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS) to expand their businesses into West African markets. The government said increased regional trade was critical to economic growth, integration and stability across the sub-region. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call at the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme Sensitisation Workshop for the North-Central zone, held in Lokoja, Kogi State, in collaboration with the ECOWAS Commission. Enikanolaiye disclosed that Nigeria had registered about 3,500 companies and 20,000 products under the scheme, but said the figures remained below the country’s potential compared with the performance of some other ECOWAS member states. He urged Nigerian businesses to exploit the scheme, which grants qualifying products originating from member countries preferential access to regional markets, to increase exports, expand production and improve the country’s competitiveness. The minister identified the agricultural potential of Kogi and other North-Central states as an opportunity to develop products for regional and international markets. He listed livestock, mangoes, millet, maize, sugar, groundnuts and cashew as commodities that could be processed into value-added products for export to other West African countries. Enikanolaiye urged participants to use the workshop to familiarise themselves with product registration procedures, rules of origin, certification and other requirements for accessing preferential markets under the scheme. “Expanding trade among African countries would not only promote economic cooperation but also strengthen relationships among nations and contribute to peace and security across the continent,” he said. The minister’s appeal comes as Kogi State seeks to position itself as a centre for regional commerce, industrial production and agricultural processing, leveraging its geographical location and natural resources. Welcoming participants, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo said the state’s location at the confluence of Rivers Niger and Benue, agricultural resources, solid mineral deposits and road networks connecting major economic centres offered significant opportunities for trade and investment. Ododo said his administration’s 32-year development plan was designed to translate these advantages into sustainable economic prosperity. He disclosed that the proposed Ajaokuta Free Trade Zone, Agro-Processing Zone and Kogi International Airport were among the strategic projects being pursued to attract investors, expand production capacity and connect local businesses to international markets. The governor also highlighted the Kogi Rebrand Initiative and Invest in Kogi campaign as efforts to showcase investment opportunities in agriculture, solid minerals, tourism and

item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses exclusion from INEC list
item.description: ……receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP in Ogun By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has dismissed the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that the development would not derail his ambition to contest the 2027 governorship election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s State Secretariat in Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital. The defectors, led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, were received by Adebutu alongside prominent PDP leaders, including the party’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would eventually be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He argued that his political history and participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades were sufficient evidence of his loyalty, challenging those questioning his membership to produce evidence of when he allegedly defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. The PDP chieftain further disclosed that he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun State, which, according to him, recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing the development as further evidence of his continued membership of the opposition party. item.title: NDLEA, Australian police sign pact against drug cartels
item.description: ….Marwa describes agreement as declaration of war on transnational traffickers By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) and the Australian Federal Police (AFP) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation against transnational drug trafficking networks operating along the Nigeria-Australia route. The agreement, signed at the NDLEA national headquarters in Abuja on Monday, November 2, 2026, formalises existing cooperation between the two agencies into a structured strategic partnership. Speaking at the ceremony, NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), described the agreement as “a declaration of war against transnational drug cartels that think they can hide between continents”. He expressed confidence that the partnership would make the Australia-Nigeria drug route hostile and unprofitable for traffickers, leveraging the AFP’s global reach and the NDLEA’s operational capacity. Under the agreement, the agencies will cooperate in four key areas: information and intelligence sharing, joint and coordinated operations, capacity building and professional development, and controlled delivery. Marwa said the pact came at a time when drug trafficking had become increasingly transnational, organised and sophisticated, with Nigerian organised crime groups allegedly linked to the Australia-Pacific drug route, particularly in the trafficking of methamphetamine and cocaine. “Nigeria is being exploited as a transit and sourcing hub, but no single country can fight this alone,” he said. He expressed hope that the agreement would lead to major joint seizures, arrests of high-value targets and successful controlled deliveries, adding that both agencies looked forward to its immediate implementation. Citing recent operations, the NDLEA boss disclosed that the agency had seized 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine intended for export and dismantled four methamphetamine laboratories in recent months, where Mexican nationals were allegedly embedded. He said one of the laboratories yielded seizures valued at more than $360 million. Marwa also cited the dismantling of a Switzerland-based cartel allegedly linked to a Nigerian, Simon Amadi, following more than a year of joint operations involving the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), as well as French, Greek and Swiss police. He said the cartel’s assets in Nigeria had also been targeted. In her remarks, leader of the AFP delegation, Ms Sandra Booth, said tackling drug trafficking required a whole-of-society approach. She commended the NDLEA for addressing different aspects of the problem, from prevention to enforcement, and described its international partnerships as commendable. Booth said the agreement would serve as a “force multiplier” in the fight against drug trafficking. She explained that organised crime groups increasingly used proceeds from drug trafficking to finance other serious crimes throug
